s1.p1: If you use the keyboard shortcut **⟦f0⟧** or the **⟦f1⟧** key, it will open up a development panel like this:
s1.p2: As you can see, there are several tabs in the development panel:
s1.p4: If you have studied layout, you are already familiar with the **Elements** tab. Here you can see the page layout and element styles.
s1.p5: However, now we will gradually learn the rest of the tabs, and we will start with the **Console** tab.
s2.p1: In the console we see the prompt **⟦f2⟧**, i.e. the console is waiting for you to enter any command, which will be executed as soon as you press **⟦f3⟧**:
s2.p2: Due to the fact that every browser has the JS engine (V8), we can execute any script directly in the console.
s2.p3: ^^If you need to enter a multi-line code fragment, at the end of each line press **⟦f4⟧** instead of **⟦f5⟧**, because **⟦f6⟧** executes the entered code immediately, and **⟦f7⟧** allows you to jump to a new line of code without starting execution.^^
s2.p4: Generally speaking, the console is intended for displaying messages when our code is being executed.
s2.p5: For example, when we encounter errors in our code, the engine will generate an **exception** and throw an error message to the console.
s2.p6: All exceptions are grouped into three main clusters:
s2.p10: Exception means interrupting code execution on the line where there is an error.
s2.p11: Moreover, we can access the console "by name" (**⟦f8⟧**) and use its commands to output some messages to the console:
s2.p12: ![ico-25 smile] We will stop studying the Developer Toolbar for now, but we will use its other tabs later on, and I hope you will appreciate the possibilities this panel provides you with.
